provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Revision of numbers 1 to 10
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers from 1 to 10.
The pupils should be able to order numbers from smallest to biggest.

Introduction:
We have learned numbers before. Today we will practice counting them.

Content:
Count numbers from 1 to 10 using fingers.
Show number cards and say each number.
Fill in missing numbers in a sequence like 1, 2, __, 4.

Class activity:
Pupils will line up and count from 1 to 10 one by one.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 1 to 10.
Which number comes after 5?
Fill the gap: 3, 4, __, 6.

Summary:
We can count and order numbers from 1 to 10.

topics.title: Numbers 11 to 15
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers 11 to 15.
The pupils should be able to write numbers 11 to 15.

Introduction:
We know numbers up to 10. Now we will learn bigger numbers.

Content:
Count numbers 11 to 15 using sticks.
Show tens and ones: 10 is one ten, 11 is one ten and one one.
Write numbers 11 to 15 on the board.

Class activity:
Pupils will bundle ten sticks together to make a ten.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 11 to 15.
How many tens in 12?
Write the number after 13.

Summary:
Numbers 11 to 15 have one ten and some ones.

topics.title: Numbers 16 to 20
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers 16 to 20.
The pupils should be able to write numbers 16 to 20.

Introduction:
We learned numbers 11 to 15. Now we will learn up to 20.

Content:
Count numbers 16 to 20 using sticks.
Show tens and ones: 16 is one ten and six ones.
Write numbers 16 to 20 on the board.

Class activity:
Pupils will bundle sticks to show numbers 16 to 20.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 16 to 20.
How many ones in 18?
Write the number before 20.

Summary:
Numbers 16 to 20 have one ten and some ones.

topics.title: Comparing numbers
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify more than.
The pupils should be able to identify less than.

Introduction:
We know numbers. Some numbers are bigger. Some are smaller.

Content:
More than means bigger number. Less than means smaller number.
Use counters to show more: 5 oranges and 3 oranges. 5 is more than 3.
Use counters to show less: 2 books and 4 books. 2 is less than 4.

Class activity:
Pupils will compare groups of stones and say which has more.

Evaluation questions:
Circle the group with more.
Circle the group with less.
Is 7 more than 4?

Summary:
We can compare numbers to find which is more or less.

topics.title: Ordering numbers
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to arrange numbers from smallest to biggest.
The pupils should be able to arrange numbers from biggest to smallest.

Introduction:
We can compare numbers. We can also put them in order.

Content:
Biggest to smallest: 10, 8, 5, 2.
Smallest to biggest: 3, 6, 9, 12.
Use number cards to show ordering.

Class activity:
Pupils will get number cards and arrange them in order.

Evaluation questions:
Arrange 5, 2, 8 from smallest to biggest.
Arrange 15, 10, 20 from biggest to smallest.
Which number is biggest: 7 or 9?

Summary:
We can order numbers from smallest to biggest or biggest to smallest.

topics.title: Addition with objects
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add two groups of objects.
The pupils should be able to count the total.

Introduction:
We can put things together. This is called addition.

Content:
Addition means putting together. Show 2 tops and 3 tops.
Count all tops: 2 + 3 = 5 tops.
Use real objects like pencils to add groups.

Class activity:
Pupils will put two groups of counters together and count them.

Evaluation questions:
Add 4 pencils and 2 pencils.
Add 3 books and 3 books.
What is 2 + 3?

Summary:
Addition means putting groups together and counting all.

topics.title: Simple addition to 10
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add numbers to 10.
The pupils should be able to write addition sums.

Introduction:
We can add objects. Now we will add numbers.

Content:
Two plus one is three. 2 + 1 = 3.
Show addition on fingers: 3 fingers up plus 2 fingers up is 5 fingers.
Write simple sums like 1 + 2 = 3.

Class activity:
Pupils will write simple addition sums in their books.

Evaluation questions:
What is 3 + 2?
What is 4 + 1?
Write 2 + 3 = .

Summary:
We can add small numbers up to 10.

topics.title: Subtraction with objects
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to take away objects.
The pupils should be able to count what is left.

Introduction:
We can add. We can also take away. This is subtraction.

Content:
Subtraction means taking away. Show 5 oranges.
Take away 2 oranges. Count what is left: 5 - 2 = 3.
Tell a story about eating some oranges.

Class activity:
Pupils will take away counters from a group and count what is left.

Evaluation questions:
Take away 2 from 5.
Take away 1 from 4.
What is 6 - 3?

Summary:
Subtraction means taking away and counting what is left.

topics.title: Simple subtraction from 10
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to subtract numbers from 10.
The pupils should be able to write subtraction sums.

Introduction:
We can subtract objects. Now we will subtract numbers.

Content:
Five take away two is three. 5 - 2 = 3.
Show subtraction on fingers: 5 fingers up, put down 2, count 3 left.
Write simple sums like 4 - 1 = 3.

Class activity:
Pupils will write simple subtraction sums in their books.

Evaluation questions:
What is 7 - 2?
What is 5 - 3?
Write 6 - 4 = .

Summary:
We can subtract small numbers from 10.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers to 20.
The pupils should be able to add and subtract small numbers.

Introduction:
Today we will practice what we learned this term.

Content:
Count numbers from 1 to 20.
Do addition sums like 3 + 2.
Do subtraction sums like 5 - 1.

Class activity:
Pupils will play a number quiz game in class.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 10 to 20.
What is 4 + 3?
What is 8 - 2?

Summary:
We have learned many things in math this term.
